tests.procedure: Under strong white light check each received sample container separately in a clean transparent watch glass or glass dish for foreign particles, colour and conformity with the visual specification.

Weigh 100 mg in a stoppered tube; add 0.1 mL solvent, shake 1 min, hold at 25.0 ± 0.5 °C for 15 min, repeat shake/hold once if not dissolved; add 0.9 mL, then 2 mL, then 7 mL solvent with the same shake and hold steps to classify very soluble / freely soluble / soluble / sparingly soluble; if still undissolved use 10 mg in 10 mL (slightly soluble), then 1 mg in 10 mL (very slightly soluble), else practically insoluble. Repeat with alcohol (ethanol 96%).

Identification: effervescence with acetic acid (carbonate). Solution of calcium carbonate 1 in 20 with 2 drops methyl red TS, neutralised with 6 N ammonium hydroxide; add 3 N hydrochloric acid dropwise until acid to the indicator; add ammonium oxalate TS: a white precipitate forms, insoluble in 6 N acetic acid but dissolving in hydrochloric acid.

Acid-insoluble substances: mix 5 g (W1) sample with 10 mL water; add hydrochloric acid dropwise with agitation until effervescence ceases; add water to 200 mL; filter; wash the residue with water until the washings show no chloride; ignite at 600 ± 50 °C; weigh the residue. % = residue / W1 x 100.

Iron (limit test): sample solution 40 mg in 5 mL 2 N hydrochloric acid, transferred and diluted with water to 10 mL; reference solution 4.0 mL standard iron solution diluted to 10 mL. Each: add 2 mL citric acid solution (1 in 5) and 2 drops thioglycolic acid; adjust to pH 9.5 ± 0.1 with ammonia TS; dilute to 20 mL, stand 5 min, dilute to 50 mL. Measure absorbance at 530 nm against water. Sample absorbance must not exceed the standard.

Lead (limit test, dithizone): sample 1.0 g in 5 mL water, add 8 mL 3 N hydrochloric acid, evaporate to dryness, dissolve in 5 mL water; add ammonium citrate and hydroxylamine hydrochloride solutions, phenol red TS, make just alkaline with ammonia, add potassium cyanide solution; extract with dithizone extraction solution; wash with dilute nitric acid; add standard dithizone and ammonium cyanide solutions, shake. Colour must not be deeper violet than a standard made with the diluted standard lead solution equivalent to the permitted lead.

details.technique: colorimetric dithizone (STM); spec sheet says AAS (see openQuestions)

tests.procedure: Arsenic (limit test): test solution 1.0 g dissolved in 15 mL hydrochloric acid, diluted to 55 mL; standard = 3.0 mL standard arsenic solution diluted to 35 mL. Add potassium iodide TS, stronger acid stannous chloride TS and isopropyl alcohol to both, stand 30 min; generate arsine with granular zinc in a scrubber (lead acetate cotton) into silver diethyldithiocarbamate TS for 45 min at room temperature. Test colour must not exceed the standard colour (optionally absorbance at 535-540 nm against the reagent blank).

details.technique: colorimetric (STM); spec sheet says AAS (see openQuestions)

tests.procedure: Barium: dip a platinum wire in the filtrate from the acid-insoluble substances test and hold it in a non-luminous flame; the flame must not show a green colour.

Fluoride (potentiometric, ion-selective electrode): sample 2.0 g dissolved in 20 mL water and 4.0 mL hydrochloric acid; add 50.0 mL solution A (294 mg/mL sodium citrate dihydrate) and water to 100 mL. Calibrate with the USP Sodium Fluoride RS standard (20.0 mL stock 1.11 mg/mL + 50.0 mL solution A, to 100 mL) and additions of 100, 100, 300, 500 µL; read potential in mV at 5 min intervals; plot log concentration (0.1, 0.2, 0.5, 1.0 µg/mL) versus mV. Result = (V x C) / W, C in µg/mL from the response line, W = sample weight (g).

details.solutionA: 294 mg/mL sodium citrate dihydrate in water
details.electrodes: fluoride-specific ion-selective electrode; silver-silver chloride reference electrode; pH meter
details.standard: USP Sodium Fluoride RS, stock 1.11 mg/mL; 20.0 mL + 50.0 mL solution A to 100.0 mL
details.formula: Result = (V x C) / W; V = volume of the sample solution (mL) (test volume of 100 mL implied, not stated), C = fluoride concentration (µg/mL), W = sample weight (g)

tests.procedure: Magnesium and alkali salts: mix 1.0 g (W) sample with 35 mL water and 3 mL hydrochloric acid; boil 1 min; add 40 mL oxalic acid TS, stir; add methyl red TS and 6 N ammonium hydroxide dropwise to just alkaline; cool; dilute to 100 mL; stand 4 h or overnight; filter. Evaporate 50 mL of filtrate in a platinum dish with 0.5 mL sulfuric acid, ignite to constant weight. % residue = weight of residue / W.

details.formula: % residue = weight of residue / W x 100

tests.procedure: Weigh a previously dried and cooled weighing bottle (W0); add 1.000 g sample (W1 = bottle + material); dry in calibrated oven at 200 °C for 4 h, cool in desiccator, weigh (W2); repeat drying to constant weight. % loss on drying = (W1 - W2) / (W1 - W0) x 100.
Bulk density: tare an empty dry cylinder; put 10 mL of bulk powder into it; weigh (W); bulk density = W / 10 mL.

details.reference: Supplier Certificate (as stated in STM); spec sheet says In-house

tests.procedure: Assay (direct complexometric titration): weigh 200 mg sample, previously dried at 200 °C for 4 h; moisten with water, dissolve with dropwise 3 N hydrochloric acid; add 100 mL water, 15 mL 1 N sodium hydroxide and 300 mg hydroxy naphthol blue; titrate with 0.05 M edetate disodium VS to a distinct blue endpoint (visual). Blank = 100 mL water + 15 mL 1 N sodium hydroxide. Assay % = ((V - B) x M x F x 100) / W, F = 100.09 mg/mmol, W in mg.

details.titrantStandardization: about 200 mg chelometric standard calcium carbonate, dried, dissolved in water and dilute HCl; titrated with edetate disodium to a blue endpoint using hydroxy naphthol blue at pH 12-13; M = (gCaCO3 x Assay/100 x 1000) / (100.09 x mL EDTA)
details.titrantPreparation: 18.6 g edetate disodium in water to 1000 mL
details.blank: 100 mL water + 15 mL 1 N sodium hydroxide
details.formula: Assay = ((V - B) x M x F x 100) / W; V = sample titrant volume (mL), B = blank titrant volume (mL), M = titrant molarity (mmol/mL), F = 100.09 mg/mmol, W = sample weight (mg)

tests.procedure: Particle size distribution: measured with a calibrated particle size analyser, reporting the mass percentage in each sieve size range; in-house specification D10 1.5 µm, D50 6 µm, D90 12 µm (10%, 50%, 90% smaller).

Total aerobic microbial count: 10 g sample + SCDB to 100 mL; within 1 h pipette 1 mL into each of 4 plates (2 SCDA, 2 SDA); incubate SCDA 24-72 h at 30-35 °C; count; CFU/g = (sum of colonies on the 2 SCDA plates / 2) x DF (10). No growth: report 'less than 10' at 1:10 dilution.
Total combined yeasts and moulds count: same preparation as TAMC; 2 SDA plates incubated 5-7 days at 20-25 °C; CFU/g = (sum of colonies on the 2 SDA plates / 2) x DF (10).

Escherichia coli: incubate SCDB 30-35 °C for 24-48 h; transfer 1 mL to 10 mL MacConkey broth (MBP), incubate 42-44 °C for 24-48 h; subculture on MacConkey agar (MAR) 30-35 °C 18-24 h; confirm by Gram stain (gram-negative short rods), EMB (dark-centred colonies), and TBX at 42-44 °C 18-72 h (blue or green colonies); optional identification system, report present if probability above 70%.
Mercury: no method stated in the STM.
